cocktails.name: El Pepino
cocktails.history: "El pepino" is Spanish for cucumber, and this cool-but-fiery Margarita riff earns the name. Muddled cucumber and fresh jalapeño give it a garden-fresh body and a slow, creeping heat, with lime, agave, and a chili-salt rim keeping it bright and balanced.
cocktails.method: Muddle the cucumber, jalapeño, and tequila in a shaker for about 10 seconds, until fully pulverized. Add the agave and lime, fill with ice, and shake 15–20 seconds until well-chilled. Double-strain through a fine-mesh strainer into a Tajín-rimmed rocks glass over fresh ice, and garnish with a cucumber slice.
cocktails.notes: The heat scales with the jalapeño — seed the wheels for a milder version.

cocktails.name: Madras
cocktails.history: Named for the brightly checked madras cloth of southern India — in the glass, the cranberry and orange streak together much the same way. It's an easygoing, brunch-friendly cooler: tart, citrusy, and barely-there boozy.
cocktails.method: Fill a highball glass with ice. Add the vodka, cranberry juice, and orange juice, give it a quick stir, and garnish with a lime wedge.

cocktails.name: Original Mai Tai
cocktails.history: Trader Vic's 1944 original — the purist's Mai Tai, with no pineapple or orange juice in sight. It leans entirely on good aged rum, fresh lime, orange curaçao, and almondy orgeat over crushed ice. As the story goes, a Tahitian friend took one sip and called it "maita'i" — out of this world.
cocktails.method: Shake the rum, lime, curaçao, orgeat, and simple syrup with crushed ice, then pour unstrained into a rocks glass. Garnish with a spent lime shell and a mint sprig.
cocktails.notes: For the rum, a blend of 1 oz amber Martinique + 1 oz dark Jamaican is classic. No orgeat? Amaretto stands in, a touch sweeter. Fresh lime only.

cocktails.name: Hawaiian Mai Tai
cocktails.history: The island-resort take on the Mai Tai — sweeter, fruitier, and built for the beach. Pineapple and orange juice join the rum, orgeat, and orange liqueur, with a float of dark rum crowning the glass. Less austere than the 1944 original; more of a sunset-on-the-lanai pour.
cocktails.method: Shake the light rum, pineapple juice, orange juice, orange liqueur, and orgeat with ice, then pour over crushed ice in a tall glass. Float the dark rum on top, and garnish with a maraschino cherry and a pineapple spear.
cocktails.notes: Orange juice is to taste — anywhere from 1/2 to 1 oz. Float the dark rum last for the dramatic dark cap.
cocktails.source: Allrecipes / tiki-bar style, via user screenshots

cocktails.name: Blueberry Lavender Vodka Spritzer
cocktails.history: A pitcher-made summer cooler built on a homemade blueberry-lavender syrup — vodka, fresh lime, and club soda do the rest. Floral and berry-bright without being sweet, it's the kind of thing you batch ahead and pour all afternoon.
cocktails.method: In a glass pitcher, stir together the vodka, blueberry-lavender syrup, lime juice, and club soda. Add ice and a handful of blueberries. Pour into glasses and garnish each with a few blueberries and a lavender sprig.
cocktails.notes: Blueberry-lavender syrup (make ahead): simmer 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar, and 1 cup blueberries with 4 fresh lavender sprigs (or 1 tbsp dried) for ~10 minutes, then strain, mashing the berries. Makes more than one batch needs — keep the extra on hand. Using dried lavender? Use 1 1/2 tsp food-grade buds in place of the sprigs.

subRecipe.name: Blueberry-lavender simple syrup
subRecipe.method: Boil water, sugar, and blueberries; stir to dissolve. Reduce to a low simmer, add lavender, simmer ~10 min. Strain, mashing the berries.

singleServing.method: Build over ice in a tall glass — vodka, syrup, and lime — then top with club soda. Add the blueberries and a lavender sprig.

cocktails.name: Spicy Margarita
cocktails.history: A Margarita with a kick — Ancho Reyes chili liqueur brings a smoky, ancho-pepper heat to the usual reposado-and-lime backbone. Agave keeps it rounded, and a chile-lime salt rim doubles down on the warmth.
cocktails.garnish: Chile-lime (or sea) salt rim + lime peel or wedge
cocktails.method: Shake with plenty of ice, then double-strain into a rocks glass. Garnish with a lime peel or wedge.
cocktails.notes: A half salt rim is a nice touch — salted sips on one side, clean on the other.

cocktails.name: Cucumber Elderflower Gimlet
cocktails.history: A garden-fresh riff on the Gimlet — gin and lime get a floral lift from elderflower and a cool, savory crunch from muddled cucumber, shaken hard and served up. Hendrick's, with its cucumber-and-rose botanicals, is the natural pour here.
cocktails.method: Fill a shaker with ice. Add the gin, elderflower liqueur, lime juice, and cucumber pieces, seal tightly, and shake hard for about 30 seconds. Strain into a martini glass and garnish with a cucumber round.
cocktails.notes: Hendrick's suits this best — its cucumber and rose-petal notes echo the drink. Use a classic dry gin only if you really love juniper, or substitute vodka.

ingredients.item: peeled cucumber, cut into ¼-inch pieces

cocktails.name: Toasted Apple Cider Bourbon Smash
cocktails.history: A cozy holiday smash — toasted bourbon and orange liqueur stirred into caramel-apple cider, sweetened with maple and dusted with cinnamon sugar. Finished with a toasted cinnamon stick, rosemary, and apple slices, it's autumn in a glass.
cocktails.garnish: Cinnamon-sugar rim, toasted cinnamon stick, rosemary sprig, apple slices
cocktails.method: Stir the bourbon, orange liqueur, maple syrup, cinnamon sugar, and caramel apple cider with ice. Strain into a cinnamon-sugar-rimmed rocks glass over fresh ice. Add apple slices, then a lightly toasted cinnamon stick and a rosemary sprig.
cocktails.notes: Calls for "toasted bourbon" — Basil Hayden Toast is the recommended bottle. Toasting the cinnamon stick and rosemary over a flame brings out the aromatics.

cocktails.name: Whiskey Sour
cocktails.history: The benchmark sour — whiskey, lemon, and a little sweetness held in perfect tension. A touch of egg white makes it silky with a cloud-white cap, and a few dashes of bitters add depth.
cocktails.method: In an ice-filled shaker, combine the whiskey, lemon juice, simple syrup, and — if using — the egg white and bitters. Shake well, then strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice (or a coupe). Garnish with an orange slice and a cherry on a pick.
cocktails.notes: New York Sour: float 3/4 oz red wine on top. Amaretto Sour: swap the whiskey for amaretto and omit the simple syrup. Gold Rush: use rich honey syrup instead of simple.
cocktails.source: Classy as F*** Cocktails (book), via user photos

cocktails.name: Whiskey Smash
cocktails.history: The Sour's leafy cousin — muddled mint and bourbon brightened with lemon and a little sweetness. Herbal, refreshing, and dead simple once you've coaxed the oils out of the mint.
cocktails.method: Muddle the mint leaves with the simple syrup in a shaker to release the oils. Add ice, the bourbon, and lemon juice, and shake until well chilled. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice and garnish with a mint sprig.
cocktails.notes: Drop the lemon and build it in a julep cup over crushed ice and you've got a Mint Julep. Rye, other whiskey, brandy, or dark rum all work in place of the bourbon.
cocktails.source: Classy as F*** Cocktails (book), via user photos

cocktails.name: Mississippi Punch
cocktails.history: A deceptively strong sipper from the 1860s — brandy out front, with bourbon and dark rum stacked behind it over lemon and a little sugar. It drinks easy and hits hard; a proper party-starter.
cocktails.garnish: Lemon or orange slice + seasonal berries
cocktails.method: Stir the sugar and lemon juice in a shaker until the sugar dissolves. Add the brandy, bourbon, and dark rum with ice and shake. Strain into an ice-filled Collins glass and garnish with a citrus slice and a few seasonal berries.
cocktails.notes: Traditionally made with cognac, but any decent brandy does the job beautifully.
cocktails.source: Classy as F*** Cocktails (book), via user photos

cocktails.name: Tom Collins / Gin Fizz
cocktails.history: Two riffs on the same fizzy lemonade-for-grown-ups: gin, lemon, and sugar shaken and lengthened with soda. A Tom Collins goes tall over ice; a Gin Fizz goes into a chilled glass with no ice, for a softer, frothier pour.
cocktails.method: Shake the gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice. For a Tom Collins, strain into an ice-filled Collins glass and top with soda. For a Gin Fizz, strain into a chilled highball with no ice and top with soda. Garnish with a lemon slice.
cocktails.notes: The only real difference is ice and volume. For an egg-rich fizz, dry-shake first: a whole egg (Royal), egg white (Silver), or yolk (Golden).
cocktails.source: Classy as F*** Cocktails (book), via user photos

cocktails.name: Bee's Knees
cocktails.history: A Prohibition-era classic built on honey — gin, lemon, and honey syrup shaken and served up. Elegant in its simplicity; the honey rounds the lemon into something golden and easy.
cocktails.method: Shake the gin, honey syrup, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with a lemon twist.
cocktails.notes: Rich honey syrup is just honey stirred with a little warm water (about 3:1). Swap the gin for white rum (Honeysuckle) or dark rum (Honeybee).
cocktails.source: Classy as F*** Cocktails (book), via user photos

cocktails.name: Fog Cutter
cocktails.history: An over-the-top tiki monster that hides its strength behind the fruit — white rum, brandy, and gin all pile in with orange, lemon, and almondy orgeat, finished with a float of nutty amontillado sherry. Strong as anything; sip slowly.
cocktails.method: Shake the rum, brandy, gin, orange juice, lemon juice, and orgeat with ice. Pour into a tiki mug with crushed ice (or an ice-filled Collins glass) and float the sherry on top. Garnish with a mint sprig and serve with a straw.
cocktails.notes: For more punch and less juice, replace the orange juice with 1/2 oz orange curaçao.
cocktails.source: Classy as F*** Cocktails (book), via user photos

cocktails.name: Mojito
cocktails.history: The easygoing benchmark cooler — muddled mint, white rum, and lime, lengthened with soda over crushed ice. Smooth, minty, and endlessly drinkable on a warm afternoon.
cocktails.method: Muddle the mint leaves in the bottom of a shaker. Add the simple syrup, lime juice, and rum, and shake. Strain into a highball glass with crushed ice and top with soda. Garnish with a mint sprig and serve with a straw.
cocktails.notes: A dash or two of Angostura is a popular addition; ginger, passion fruit, or pineapple are all nice in the muddle. Top with dry sparkling wine instead of soda if you're feeling fancy.
cocktails.source: Classy as F*** Cocktails (book), via user photos

cocktails.name: Aperol Spritz
cocktails.history: Italy's golden hour in a glass — bittersweet Aperol lengthened with dry sparkling wine and a splash of soda over ice. Light, fizzy, and just bitter enough; the quintessential warm-weather aperitivo.
cocktails.method: Fill a wine glass with ice. Add the sparkling wine, Aperol, and soda, and stir gently to combine. Garnish with an orange slice.
cocktails.notes: Swap the Aperol for another Italian amaro — Cappelletti, Montenegro, even Pimm's — for a different spritz. Or replace the sparkling wine with ginger ale, rhubarb soda, or bitter lemon.
cocktails.source: Classy as F*** Cocktails (book), via user photos
